slides.title: 25,494 earthquakes across 12 authoritative regional networks
slides.caption: 11 August–10 November 2026 UTC. U.S. ANSS authoritative regional networks, all magnitudes. Magnitude scales differ among providers.
slides.notes: The primary grouping is the catalog preferred origin network, an operational proxy for authority. USGS preferences include geographic authority, source and update time. These volumes measure the ComCat cohort, not each network’s entire local catalog.

slides.title: Magnitude coverage differs across network cohorts
slides.caption: Bins are left-inclusive and right-exclusive. Preferred catalog magnitudes determine event-count strata. Counts overlap neither networks nor bins.

slides.title: Automatic submissions and review coverage
slides.caption: Observed publication comes from archived origin versions. Absence of retained automatic history does not prove that a network never publishes automatically.
slides.notes: Coverage: 25,494 histories from 25,494 cohort events. Paired events: 9,754. Archive acquisition uses the documented PDL west products_created_after stream and cached pilot FDSN detail responses.

slides.caption: Earliest retained automatic origin versus latest reviewed origin from the same network and product code. Revisions measure change, not independent accuracy.

slides.title: Interpretation and reproducibility
paragraphs: Catalog volume and magnitude range describe different earthquake populations and reporting thresholds.
Automatic-to-reviewed changes quantify revisions. Independent ground truth would be needed to rank location accuracy.
Pick metadata and uncertainty conventions constrain comparisons. Unknown values remain explicit.
The GitHub repository contains event tables, paired product IDs, methods, publication figures and the frozen archive snapshot.
slides.caption: All network comparisons are descriptive. Full distributions and per-metric sample sizes accompany every summary.
